page: Amazon Web Services c6i.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized instance powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, accompanied by a 54 MB L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic acceleration. It includes 256 GB of DDR4 system memory clocked at 3 GHz, establishing a 2 GB per core ratio typical of compute-oriented architectures. The platform features no discrete GPU hardware and contains no bundled local disk storage, relying on external network-attached storage via its 50 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark testing demonstrates high throughput across parallelized compute pipelines. The system scores in the top tier for PassMark CPU evaluation (87,633.32), CPU encryption (112,450.63), and Geekbench ray tracing (96,153.0). Clang compilation workloads reach 54,938.0 points, and multi-core Geekbench reaches 17,789.0 points, reflecting strong multi-threaded scaling. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth measures at 337.58 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core (1,909.79) and Geekbench single-core (1,685.0), rank within the middle tier.

Without hypervisor virtualization overhead, the instance delivers predictable, dedicated compute capacity. The primary tradeoff lies in the absence of onboard NVMe storage, meaning all disk I/O depends on network-attached volumes, and memory density remains restricted to 2 GB per thread. The hardware allocation delivers high cost efficiency for highly parallel, CPU-bound workloads where memory capacity requirements are moderate. The c6i.metal server is well suited for continuous integration and large code compilation suites, distributed batch processing, static web serving clusters, and multi-threaded simulation or rendering pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c6i.metal is a compute-optimized bare-metal server configured with 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs via Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance pairs high compute density with 256 GB of DDR4 system memory at a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage and discrete GPUs, routing all storage operations through external block networks supported by a 50 Gbps baseline interface. Benchmark results reflect top-tier multi-threaded compute, encryption, and ray tracing performance, alongside strong software compilation throughput and memory bandwidth exceeding 337 GB/s uncached. While single-threaded tasks perform at moderate levels, parallel execution scales effectively without hypervisor overhead. The platform provides strong resource density and compute efficiency for intensive parallel tasks, making it suited for large-scale software builds, batch computation, video rendering, and high-throughput static web serving.
